evidence.source: Demystifying the Memory System of Modern Datacenter FPGAs for Software Programmers through Microbenchmarking, FPGA 2021
evidence.measurement: Random 4-byte off-chip access at 300 MHz: HBM2 ~108 ns, DDR4 ~110 ns on tested platform.
evidence.applicability: STRONGLY_SUPPORTED order-of-magnitude latency calibration; FPGA/HLS interconnect and page-hit methodology prevent direct transfer to custom HBM4 ASIC.

evidence.source: Demystifying the Characteristics of High Bandwidth Memory for Real-Time Systems, ICCAD 2021
evidence.measurement: Pointer-chasing-like latency workload exhibits low locality and does not benefit materially from HBM peak bandwidth.
evidence.applicability: STRONGLY_SUPPORTED qualitative calibration for dependent-access workloads; not DP6 throughput measurement.

evidence.source: TrendForce HBM Supply Constraints Persist, 2027 Price Outlook Revised Upward, 2026-09-29
evidence.measurement: HBM remains supply-constrained; base-die cost does not scale proportionally with DRAM layer count; absolute transferable procurement price not publicly exposed.
evidence.applicability: Supports keeping installed HBM/package cost UNKNOWN rather than inventing $/GB.

latency_sensitivity_with_36gb_context_an.interpretation: Latency-only ceilings ignore compute/bandwidth/power and do not represent achieved DP6 throughput. They show that plausible HBM dependent latency alone does not force aggregate throughput near commodity-browser rates when many contexts are resident.

pricing_gate.reason: Public trend/forecast evidence establishes scarcity and relative cost structure, not a defensible transferable procurement lower bound.

disposition_effect: Memory latency remains a real specialization burden, but neither measured HBM2 latency nor public pricing evidence closes the commodity-viability inequality.
